item.title: A multi-method Antarctic atmospheric blocking dataset (1979–2024)
item.dc:creator: Deniz Bozkurt, Charlie Opazo, Julio C. Marín, Kyle R. Clem, Benjamin Pohl, Victoire Buffet, … (+3)
item.description:
Earth System Science Data — matched: Antarctic, Antarctica, reanalysis, extreme event
Atmospheric blocking near Antarctica drives long lasting circulation anomalies and extreme events, yet it remains poorly understood. We created a new public dataset for 1979 to 2024 using global reanalysis data and several detection methods applied in a consistent way. We found strong method dependent differences in how often, where, and how long blocking occurs, showing that no single approach captures all forms of Antarctic blocking.

item.title: Biogeochemistry-Informed Neural Network (BINN v1.0) for improving accuracy of model prediction and scientific understanding of soil organic carbon storage
item.dc:creator: Haodi Xu, Joshua Fan, Feng Tao, Lifen Jiang, Fengqi You, Benjamin Houlton, … (+3)
item.description:
Geoscientific Model Development — matched: Bayesian, neural network
We developed the Biogeochemistry-Informed Neural Network (BINN) which embeds a process-based model inside an AI framework so the model’s parameters can be learned from empirical data. BINN could recover prescribed parameters in synthetic tests and retrieve key processes controlling the modeled soil organic carbon when applied to ~25 000 soil profiles in US. It operates more than 50 times faster than the traditional Bayesian approach for data-model integration.

item.title: The Arctic Radiation-Cloud-Aerosol-Surface Interaction Experiment (ARCSIX) airborne campaign dataset
item.dc:creator: Patrick C. Taylor, Armin Sorooshian, Rei Ueyama, Sebastian Schmidt, Ihab Abboud, Quincy Allison, … (+123)
item.description:
Earth System Science Data — matched: Arctic, sea ice
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments) This article summarizes the data sets collected during the Arctic Radiation Cloud aerosol Sea ice Interaction eXperiment (ARCSIX), NASA's most comprehensive Arctic field campaign to date. The overarching goal was to quantify the contributions of surface, clouds, aerosol particles, and precipitation to summer sea ice melt. This paper describes the ARCSIX implementation including the flight strategy, instruments, complementary data sets, access, and usage details.

item.title: Assessing the effect of land cover on ISBA snow water equivalent and land surface temperature simulations over Europe
item.dc:creator: Oscar Rojas-Munoz, Constantin Ardilouze, Bertrand Bonan, Diane Tzanos, Darren Ghent, Céline Lamarche, … (+2)
item.description:
The Cryosphere
This study evaluated how updating land cover maps, such as forests, grasslands, and croplands, affects simulations of snow and land surface temperatures across Europe from 2010 to 2022. Results using older, less detailed maps were compared with those from newer, high-resolution data. The updated maps improved the accuracy of snow predictions, particularly in areas where grasslands transitioned to forests. However, the improvements were less noticeable for temperature simulations.
